q:
Statement :
Do not copy our software without our permission - A notice

Assumptions :
I. It is possible to copy the software.
II. Such warning will have some effect.
o: if only assumption I is implicit
if only assumption II is implicit
if neither of the assumptions is implicit
if both the assumptions are implicit
e:
Both the assumptions are implicit. 
If it was not possible to copy the software, such statement would not have made. 
The warning is given because it may have some effect. 
Thus assumptions I and II are implicit.

q:
Statement : “
We need to appoint more teachers” – Principal informs the school staff.

Assumptions : 
I. Teachers are available. 
II. Present teachers are not good.
o: if only assumption I is implicit
if only assumption II is implicit
if either I or II is implicit
if neither I nor II is implicit
e:
School requires more teachers. 
It is assumed in the light of statement that teachers are available but it cannot be said that present staff of teachers is not good. 
Hence, only assumption I is implicit.

q:
Statement : 
A good executive has to be task – oriented as well as people-oriented.

Assumptions :
 I. Some executives are people-oriented.
 II. Some executives are not people-oriented.
o: if only assumption I is implicit
if only assumption II is implicit
if neither I nor II is implicit
if both I and II are implicit
e:
The statement advises that an executive should be task-oriented as well as people-oriented. 
It is based on the assumptions that some executives are only people-oriented and some executives are only task-oriented.
Hence, none of the assumptions follows.

q:
Statement : 
The private bus services in the city has virtually collapsed because of the on going strike of its employees.

Assumptions :
I. Going on strike has become the right of every employee.
II. People no more require the services of private bus operators.
o: if only assumption I is implicit
if only assumption II is implicit
if neither of the assumptions is implicit
if either assumption I or assumption II is implicit
e:
Assumption I is not at all related to the statement just because private bus operators have gone on strike does not mean that every employee has a right to go for strike (even though it may be true legally, but it is not relevant in this statement). 
Assumption II is totally irrelevant, hence both the assumptions are not implicit.

q:
Statement:
Banks should always check financial status before lending money to a client.

Assumptions : 
I. Checking before lending would give a true picture of the client's financial status.
II. Clients some times may not present the correct picture of their ability to repay loan amount to the bank.
o: If only assumption I is Implicit
If only assumption II is Implicit
If either I or II is Implicit
If both I and II are Implicit
e:
I is implicit in the norm prescribed in the sentence.
This is why checking is being advised. Again, what would the banks check? Obviously  what the clients reveal. 
Banks would assume the revelation to be true.Hence II is not implicit. 
However, II is vague. If cross - checking is what the speaker has in mind, II would become implicit.

Assumptions :
I. It is possible to measure the quality of human resources of a Nation.
II. Achieving economic prosperity is a cherished goal of any nation.
o: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Either I or II is implicit

e:

So it is not implicit.

q:
Statement: 
The company has recently announced a series of incentives to the employees who are punctual and sincere.

Assumptions:
Those who are not punctual at present may get motivated by the announcement.
The productivity of the company may increase.
The profit earned by the company may be more than the amount to be spent for the incentive programmes.
o: Only I and II are implicit
Only II and III are implicit
All are implicit
None is implicit
e:
Announcing incentives for punctual and sincere employees would surely motivate more and more employees to be punctual, and this will ensure productivity. 
So, both I and II are implicit. 
However, the statement does not give any information about the profit earned by the company. 
So, III is not implicit.

q:
Statement: 
If you are an engineer, we have a challenging job for you.

Assumptions:
We need an engineer.
You are an engineer.
o: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Either I or II is implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
e:
Clearly, job is offered to an engineer. 
This means that he is needed. So, I is implicit. 
The word 'If' in the statement makes II not implicit.
